name: Natural Hydraulic Lime Mortar (NHL 2 / NHL 3.5)
traditional_use: Modern standard conservation mortar for structural masonry, foundation consolidation, and damp subterranean repointing where traditional slaking pits are unavailable.

moisture_behavior.drying_rate: Rapid drying preventing trapped moisture accumulation
moisture_behavior.summary: Maintains breathability of historic stone masonry while setting reliably in damp subterranean conditions.

mechanical_characteristics.ductility: Moderate ductility with good elastic recovery
mechanical_characteristics.sacrificial_behavior: Sacrificial relative to medium and hard sandstones/quartzites
mechanical_characteristics.summary: Provides predictable initial hydraulic set without exceeding historic stone strength.

thermal_characteristics.compatibility_with_historic_stones: Coefficient of thermal expansion compatible with historic sandstones
thermal_characteristics.summary: Minimizes thermal fatigue at the stone-mortar interface.

chemical_considerations.soluble_salts_risk: Very low; manufactured without gypsum or synthetic additives
chemical_considerations.reactivity_with_limestone: Chemical set via calcium silicates followed by long-term carbonation
chemical_considerations.summary: Free of deleterious free alkalis; low sulfate content.

reversibility.extraction_method: Soft mechanical joint raking without substrate injury

heritage_compatibility.iks_alignment: Modern standardized equivalent of traditional hydraulic kankar lime; preserves breathability and mechanical compatibility
heritage_compatibility.asi_intach_compliance: Widely endorsed in international (ICOMOS/RILEM) and modern Indian heritage conservation practice

limitations: NHL 5.0 (eminently hydraulic) must be avoided as its high compressive strength (>10 MPa) violates sacrificiality on soft sandstones.
Must be matched with clean, well-graded local river sand aggregates.
